Fish eagles, flamingos and carmine bee-eaters, depending on the season, with a guide who knows the calls. Lunch is included. Guided in English. Runs all year round.

name: Der Nachthimmel über Springbok
description: Warme Jacke mitbringen, Wüstennächte werden kalt, und die Milchstraße ist mit bloßem Auge zu sehen. Einer der dunkelsten Himmel der Erde: Ein Astronom führt Sie mit dem Teleskop durch die Sternbilder des Südens. Keine Kondition nötig. Zwischen den Blicken durchs Teleskop sitzen wir am Feuer, mit heißer Schokolade. Am schönsten nach dem Sommerregen. Wasser und ein kleiner Imbiss sind inklusive. Führung auf Deutsch und Englisch.

name: Paddle the water at Okavango Delta
description: Stable double kayaks make this easy for first-timers, and curious seals often swim right under the hull. We launch in the calm of the morning before the wind rises and paddle along the shoreline with a guide. Everything is provided, including dry bags and a hot drink when we land. Guided in English and Afrikaans. Runs all year round. We meet at the park gate.

name: Fishing with a guide: Okavango Delta
description: Your guide knows the channels and tides, and teaches beginners without any fuss. Catch and release is encouraged, and lunch is packed for the day. Rods, bait and licences are arranged. Expect kob and steenbras on the coast, and tigerfish on the rivers. A good fit for families: short stretches and plenty to keep kids interested. Best in the dry months from May to October. Guided in English and German. Hotel transfers can be arranged.

name: Night sky session near Waterberg Plateau
description: Bring a warm jacket, since desert nights get cold, and see the Milky Way with the naked eye. No fitness needed. We sit by the fire between looks through the telescope, with hot chocolate. Some of the darkest skies on Earth: an astronomer guides you through the southern constellations with a telescope. Pick-up from your lodge is included. At its finest after the summer rains. Children are welcome, and guides adapt the pace for younger travellers. Guided in English.

name: Cape Town dune quad adventure
description: An adrenaline ride through coastal dune fields, with helmets, a briefing and stops on the highest ridges. Automatic quads are easy to handle after a short practice, and the guide adjusts the route to the group. We meet at the park gate. Guided in English and German. Runs all year round.

name: Twyfelfontein rock art walk
description: The path is uneven but short, with plenty of stops and shade at the main panels. A local guide explains how San hunter-gatherers passed on knowledge through these engravings. A short walk between sandstone slabs carved thousands of years ago with animals, footprints and maps of waterholes. Runs all year round. Guided in English. We meet at the park gate.

name: Sunrise climb at Sesriem
description: Walk the ridge barefoot if you like, then slide down the steep face and cross the white clay pan. Expect loose sand underfoot and a real effort on the final stretch, rewarded by long shadows across the sea of dunes. We set out before dawn and climb a crest of soft red sand while the valley below turns from grey to orange. Guided in English. Runs all year round. Not recommended for children under 12. We meet at the park gate.

name: Night sky session near Spitzkoppe
description: Bring a warm jacket, since desert nights get cold, and see the Milky Way with the naked eye. No fitness needed. We sit by the fire between looks through the telescope, with hot chocolate. Some of the darkest skies on Earth: an astronomer guides you through the southern constellations with a telescope. Includes water and a light snack. Guided in English. Children are welcome, and guides adapt the pace for younger travellers. At its finest after the summer rains.

name: Light aircraft over Katima Mulilo
description: The pilot narrates the geology on the way, and low passes make the scale of the landscape obvious. A small high-wing plane gives every passenger a window seat for the patterns you can't read from the ground. No walking at all, which suits anyone who wants the view without the effort. Includes water and a light snack. Runs all year round. Children are welcome, and guides adapt the pace for younger travellers. Guided in English.

name: Felsmalereien bei Spitzkoppe
description: Ein kurzer Weg zwischen Sandsteinplatten, vor Jahrtausenden mit Tieren, Fußspuren und Karten von Wasserstellen graviert. Ein einheimischer Guide erklärt, wie die San ihr Wissen über diese Gravuren weitergaben. Kinder sind willkommen, der Guide passt das Tempo an die Jüngsten an. Führung auf Deutsch und Englisch. Am schönsten in der Trockenzeit von Mai bis Oktober. Abholung von Ihrer Lodge ist inklusive.

name: Abandoned places and light: Otjiwarongo
description: Small groups and early access mean clean frames with nobody else in the picture. Bring any camera, even a phone. An evening review of your images is included. Pick-up from your lodge is included. Guided in English and Afrikaans. Best in the dry months from May to October.

name: Dorfbesuch bei Rundu
description: Bitte vor dem Fotografieren fragen. Kinder sind willkommen und spielen meist bald miteinander. Ein Übersetzer stellt Sie vor, Sie erfahren mehr über Viehzucht, Handwerk und den Alltag der Familie. Von der Gemeinde selbst organisiert: Die Einnahmen gehen direkt ans Dorf, und Sie sind Gast in einem Zuhause, nicht bei einer Show. Führung auf Deutsch. Das ganze Jahr über möglich. Kinder sind willkommen, der Guide passt das Tempo an die Jüngsten an. Abholung von Ihrer Lodge ist inklusive.

name: Sternenbeobachtung bei Kolmannskuppe
description: Einer der dunkelsten Himmel der Erde: Ein Astronom führt Sie mit dem Teleskop durch die Sternbilder des Südens. Keine Kondition nötig. Zwischen den Blicken durchs Teleskop sitzen wir am Feuer, mit heißer Schokolade. Treffpunkt ist das Parktor. Führung auf Deutsch und Englisch. Das ganze Jahr über möglich.

name: Walvis Bay food walk
description: Small tastings at family-run places where visitors rarely find their own way. Grilled kapana from the market, fresh oysters and local craft beer, with vegetarian choices arranged on request. Come hungry and expect to walk slowly, since most of the time is spent at the table. Includes water and a light snack. Guided in English. Runs all year round.

name: Paddeln in Epupa-Fälle
description: Stabile Zweierkajaks machen es auch Anfängern leicht, und neugierige Robben tauchen oft direkt unter dem Boot hindurch. Alles ist inklusive, auch wasserdichte Taschen und ein heißes Getränk nach der Landung. Führung auf Deutsch und Englisch. Das ganze Jahr über möglich. Wasser und ein kleiner Imbiss sind inklusive.

name: Night sky session near Naukluft Mountains
description: No fitness needed. We sit by the fire between looks through the telescope, with hot chocolate. Some of the darkest skies on Earth: an astronomer guides you through the southern constellations with a telescope. At its finest after the summer rains. Hotel transfers can be arranged. Guided in English. A good fit for families: short stretches and plenty to keep kids interested.

name: Cape Cross by sea kayak
description: Stable double kayaks make this easy for first-timers, and curious seals often swim right under the hull. Everything is provided, including dry bags and a hot drink when we land. We launch in the calm of the morning before the wind rises and paddle along the shoreline with a guide. At its finest after the summer rains. Guided in English. Pick-up from your lodge is included. A good fit for families: short stretches and plenty to keep kids interested.

name: On foot after black rhino: Okaukuejo
description: Conservation fees from each trip support the community rangers who protect these animals. Group sizes stay small and everyone follows the tracker's signals, since the rhino decides how close we get. Local trackers read the spoor from the vehicle, then we continue quietly on foot over rocky ground. Includes water and a light snack. Runs all year round. Guided in English.

name: Upington from the air
description: A small high-wing plane gives every passenger a window seat for the patterns you can't read from the ground. No walking at all, which suits anyone who wants the view without the effort. The pilot narrates the geology on the way, and low passes make the scale of the landscape obvious. Best in the dry months from May to October. Hotel transfers can be arranged. Guided in English.

name: Quad-Tour durch die Dünen bei Sossusvlei
description: Automatik-Quads sind nach kurzer Übung leicht zu fahren, und der Guide passt die Route der Gruppe an. Ein Adrenalinkick durch die Dünenfelder, mit Helm, Einweisung und Stopps auf den höchsten Kämmen. Mittagessen ist inklusive. Am schönsten nach dem Sommerregen. Führung auf Deutsch und Englisch.

name: Birding with a specialist at Skeleton Coast
description: A spotting scope is provided, and the pace is slow enough for keen photographers. Fish eagles, flamingos and carmine bee-eaters, depending on the season, with a guide who knows the calls. We keep a list of everything seen and send it to you afterwards. Includes water and a light snack. At its finest after the summer rains. Guided in English and German.

name: Colonial history of Swakopmund
description: German colonial architecture, the independence story and a coffee stop, all on flat and paved streets. An honest account of the country's history, including the genocide of the Herero and Nama, told by a local historian. Short distances and many benches make this a good choice for older travellers and for wheelchair users. Best in the dry months from May to October. Guided in English. Includes water and a light snack. Fully wheelchair accessible, including vehicle access and an adapted restroom.

name: Steep trails of Naukluft Mountains
description: Carry at least three litres of water. The guide sets a steady pace and watches the heat closely. A demanding walk with scrambling over boulders, long climbs and little shade, for hikers who are properly fit. Guided in English and Afrikaans. Minimum age is 14, because of the distance and terrain. Hotel transfers can be arranged. At its finest after the summer rains.

name: Tracking desert rhino near Naukluft Mountains
description: Group sizes stay small and everyone follows the tracker's signals, since the rhino decides how close we get. Conservation fees from each trip support the community rangers who protect these animals. Guided in English and German. Runs all year round. Pick-up from your lodge is included.

name: Sonnenuntergangsfahrt: Viktoriafälle
description: Über einen ebenen Steg an Bord, die ganze Fahrt über sitzen, Toilette an Bord. Pelikane begleiten das Boot, und die Crew weiß, wo diese Woche Delfine und Robben gesichtet wurden. Schattiges Deck, Snacks und kalte Getränke: die entspannteste Art, Flusspferde, Vögel und das Abendlicht zu erleben. Hoteltransfers können organisiert werden. Das ganze Jahr über möglich. Führung auf Deutsch und Englisch.

name: Stargazing at Twyfelfontein
description: Some of the darkest skies on Earth: an astronomer guides you through the southern constellations with a telescope. Bring a warm jacket, since desert nights get cold, and see the Milky Way with the naked eye. No fitness needed. We sit by the fire between looks through the telescope, with hot chocolate. Guided in English and German. Hotel transfers can be arranged. Best in the dry months from May to October.

name: On the water at Skeleton Coast
description: A shaded deck, snacks and cold drinks make this the gentlest way to watch hippos, birds and the evening light. Pelicans follow the boat, and the crew knows where dolphins and seals have been seen that week. Lunch is included. Guided in English and German. At its finest after the summer rains.

name: Windhoek on foot with a historian
description: Short distances and many benches make this a good choice for older travellers and for wheelchair users. An honest account of the country's history, including the genocide of the Herero and Nama, told by a local historian. Guided in English and Afrikaans. Best in the dry months from May to October. Includes water and a light snack.

The pilot narrates the geology on the way, and low passes make the scale of the landscape obvious. Guided in English. Hotel transfers can be arranged. Fully wheelchair accessible, including vehicle access and an adapted restroom. A good fit for families: short stretches and plenty to keep kids interested. Best in the dry months from May to October.

name: Skeleton Coast from the air
description: No walking at all, which suits anyone who wants the view without the effort. The pilot narrates the geology on the way, and low passes make the scale of the landscape obvious. Guided in English and Afrikaans. Runs all year round. A good fit for families: short stretches and plenty to keep kids interested. We meet at the park gate.

name: Photography workshop at Naukluft Mountains
description: A professional photographer helps with composition and exposure, and timing is built around the best light. Bring any camera, even a phone. An evening review of your images is included. Best in the dry months from May to October. Guided in English. Includes water and a light snack.

name: Sunrise climb at Sesriem
description: Expect loose sand underfoot and a real effort on the final stretch, rewarded by long shadows across the sea of dunes. Walk the ridge barefoot if you like, then slide down the steep face and cross the white clay pan. Lunch is included. Best in the dry months from May to October. Guided in English.

name: Birding with a specialist at Cape Cross
description: We keep a list of everything seen and send it to you afterwards. A spotting scope is provided, and the pace is slow enough for keen photographers. Guided in English and Afrikaans. Includes water and a light snack. Children are welcome, and guides adapt the pace for younger travellers. Best in the dry months from May to October.

name: Cape Town by sea kayak
description: Everything is provided, including dry bags and a hot drink when we land. Stable double kayaks make this easy for first-timers, and curious seals often swim right under the hull. We launch in the calm of the morning before the wind rises and paddle along the shoreline with a guide. Guided in English. Runs all year round. Includes water and a light snack. A good fit for families: short stretches and plenty to keep kids interested.

name: Sunset cruise at Victoria Falls
description: Pelicans follow the boat, and the crew knows where dolphins and seals have been seen that week. A shaded deck, snacks and cold drinks make this the gentlest way to watch hippos, birds and the evening light. Step aboard from a level jetty and stay seated for the whole trip, with a toilet on board. Runs all year round. Lunch is included. Guided in English. A good fit for families: short stretches and plenty to keep kids interested.

name: Game drive in Victoria Falls
description: Binoculars and a field guide are on board, and the guide tracks sightings by radio with other vehicles. Lions are most active early, so we leave at the gate's opening and stop often for photographs. Hotel transfers can be arranged. A good fit for families: short stretches and plenty to keep kids interested. At its finest after the summer rains. Guided in English and German.

name: Spitzmaulnashörner zu Fuß bei Etosha-Nationalpark
description: Die Gruppen bleiben klein und alle folgen den Handzeichen des Fährtenlesers, denn das Nashorn bestimmt den Abstand. Einheimische Fährtenleser lesen die Spuren vom Fahrzeug aus, danach geht es leise zu Fuß über steiniges Gelände weiter. Führung auf Deutsch und Englisch. Mittagessen ist inklusive. Mindestalter 14 Jahre, wegen Strecke und Gelände. Am schönsten nach dem Sommerregen.

name: On foot after black rhino: Damaraland
description: Local trackers read the spoor from the vehicle, then we continue quietly on foot over rocky ground. Group sizes stay small and everyone follows the tracker's signals, since the rhino decides how close we get. Conservation fees from each trip support the community rangers who protect these animals. Best in the dry months from May to October. Minimum age is 14, because of the distance and terrain. Includes water and a light snack. Guided in English and Afrikaans.

name: Deadvlei before the crowds
description: Skeletal camel thorn trees, nine centuries dead, stand on cracked pale clay under walls of rust-coloured sand. We reach the gate at opening so you can photograph them with nobody in the frame.

name: Inside the Sesriem gorge
description: The Tsauchab river cut this narrow slot through ancient gravel. Clamber down to pools that hold water long after the rains, and look up at layered conglomerate thirty metres overhead.

name: Tandem skydive above the Atlantic
description: Freefall for half a minute from ten thousand feet with desert on one side and cold ocean on the other. Your instructor handles everything, and all you must do is arch your back and breathe.

name: Little Five in the living desert
description: Sidewinder adders, palmato geckos and transparent lizards hide in what looks like empty sand. Our tracker reads tiny marks on the slip faces and gently brings these creatures into view.

name: Mondesa township with a resident guide
description: Meet a Damara family, try omajova mushrooms, and hear click languages spoken at a neighbourhood bar. Your host grew up on these streets and walks you round the places she actually uses.

name: Lagoon flamingos and oyster farm
description: Thousands of pink birds feed in the shallows of a RAMSAR wetland, and pelicans glide past the catamaran. Fresh oysters and sparkling wine are served on deck as the fog burns away.

name: Sandwich Harbour by four-by-four
description: Our driver reads the tide and races along the strip where towering dunes plunge straight into the surf. It's a roller coaster for grown-ups, with a picnic among seabirds at the far end.

name: Katutura market and kapana grills
description: Oshetu market smells of woodsmoke and spice. Taste strips of flame-grilled beef with chilli salt, buy mopane worms if you dare, and learn how the township came to exist under apartheid removals.

name: Independence museum and Christuskirche
description: A brisk, thoughtful hour through the capital's contested monuments, from the golden museum built by North Korean contractors to the sandstone church of the colonial era.

name: Daan Viljoen sunrise ridge walk
description: Just twenty minutes from the city, red hartebeest and mountain zebra graze the Khomas hills. A marked route rises to a viewpoint where we stop for coffee from a flask.

name: Full day across the great white pan
description: A salt pan visible from space, shimmering at the horizon. Long, unhurried hours in a raised vehicle bring zebra herds, gemsbok and with luck a cheetah resting beneath a shepherd's tree.

name: Floodlit waterhole after dark
description: Sit on a bench behind a low wall as black rhino and elephants come to drink under the lights. Whispering is the only rule, and you needn't move a muscle for the whole evening.

name: The old German fort at Namutoni
description: A whitewashed fort with a turbulent past, and a tower with long views across the Fischer pan. A ranger talks through the battles fought here and how a garrison turned into a rest camp.

name: Five days through Africa's great gorge
description: Eighty-five kilometres with everything on your back, sleeping on the riverbed under the stars. You need a doctor's certificate to enter, and only the winter months are open at all.

name: Canyon rim at sunset
description: A short drive and an easy stroll to the main viewpoint, where a drop of half a kilometre turns purple in the last light. Sundowners and biltong on a folding table.

name: Thermal springs and a slow soak
description: Hot mineral water rises at the southern end of the gorge. Spend the afternoon floating in the outdoor pool, with step-free access and a hoist, after a short nature talk.

name: Art Nouveau houses of a diamond town
description: Pastel gables and a hilltop church seem lost at the edge of the Namib. Climb to the Goerke Haus, built for a diamond magnate who barely lived in it, and hear the boom-and-bust story.

name: Sailing to Halifax Island penguins
description: A wooden schooner carries you past the guano platforms to a colony of African penguins. It gets choppy and cold beyond the point, so seasick pills and a windbreaker are wise.

name: Ghost town drowned in sand
description: Dunes pour through the doors of abandoned villas in this former diamond settlement. Wander the bowling alley and the hospital, each room a study in peeling wallpaper and drifting grains.

name: A UNESCO gallery in sandstone
description: Over two thousand figures chipped into rock, among them a lion with human paws. The site guide decodes shamanic meanings along a rough staircase path that climbs the valley.

name: Desert elephants of the Huab
description: Elephants here have longer legs and walk huge distances between dry riverbeds. We follow fresh tracks along the Huab with a researcher who knows each bull by name.

name: Organ Pipes and Burnt Mountain
description: Volcanic dolerite columns stand like a giant's instrument, and a blackened hill glows at dusk. Geology made friendly, with stops short enough for small children and grandparents.

name: Roped ascent of Namibia's Matterhorn
description: Granite friction climbing up a 1,700 metre inselberg, with a certified mountain guide and full rope work. Prior multi-pitch experience is essential, and we start in the dark to beat the heat.

name: Natural arches at golden hour
description: Giant rounded boulders form a window framing the whole plain. Short scrambles only, plenty of time with a tripod, and a fireside meal once the stars come out.

name: Fly-in shipwreck expedition
description: A small plane lands on gravel flats beside rusting hulls and whale bones. Two nights at a remote camp, with roaring seal colonies and fog that rolls in without warning.

name: A hundred thousand fur seals
description: The noise reaches you before the sight and the smell soon after. Wooden boardwalks run through the colony, level all the way, and pups tumble right beneath the railings in December.

name: Himba homestead with a Himba guide
description: Learn about red ochre, sacred fires and cattle wealth from a guide who grew up in this village. Bring maize meal rather than sweets, and the elders may share their news with you.

name: Kunene whitewater rafting
description: Grade three rapids along the Angolan border, in inflatable rafts with safety kayakers. Crocodiles bask on the far bank, so you stay in the boat on the calm stretches.

name: Baobabs above the falls
description: The Kunene splits into dozens of channels and drops into a misty gorge, framed by ancient baobabs and fig trees. Walk the rim at sunset with a local guide and a cold drink.

name: Woodcarvers of the Kavango
description: Watch craftsmen shape kiaat wood into bowls and mokoro canoes at a roadside workshop, then try a chisel yourself. Afterwards, a family lunch of fish and mahangu porridge by the river.

name: Mahango and the Bwabwata floodplain
description: Roan and sable antelope come to the lush edge of the Okavango here. It's among the richest patches in the country and very lightly visited, with big herds of buffalo in the dry season.

name: Tigerfish on the Zambezi
description: Fight the toothy river predator from an aluminium boat on the mighty Zambezi. Tackle provided, and a cooler of cold drinks. Your skipper has worked these eddies for twenty years.

name: Sandstone climb to the plateau rim
description: A shaded path through fig and wild olive trees leads up to red cliffs, where Cape vultures circle. It's a steady hour's effort and a breath of green after the dry plains.

name: The battlefield and the graves
description: In 1904, German forces defeated the Herero here and drove survivors into the desert. A descendant walks you through the cemetery and tells what the official plaques leave out.

name: Cheetah conservation behind the scenes
description: Meet the researchers running the world's largest cheetah recovery effort, see Anatolian guard dogs at work, and watch a feeding run. Level paths, and proceeds fund the programme.

name: Copper town museum and minerals
description: Rare crystals found nowhere else on earth, salvaged German weapons from Lake Otjikoto, and a mine that shaped this tidy northern town. Air-conditioned, and pleasantly unhurried.

name: The quiver tree forest
description: Hundreds of strange aloes with golden bark stand among dolerite boulders, best at sunset. Nearby, the Giant's Playground looks as if someone stacked rocks for fun.

name: Two days on the Olive Trail and beyond
description: Chains help you down a narrow gorge on the way through dolomite ridges, and mountain zebra watch from above. A proper hiker's outing with a rough overnight camp.

name: Kalahari red dunes by sundowner truck
description: Low parallel dunes the colour of paprika, oryx silhouettes and a gin and tonic on the crest. A gentle farm drive that needs nothing from you except an appetite for sunsets.

name: Elephants at the river's edge
description: Herds of hundreds swim across to Sedudu Island at dusk, trunks raised like snorkels. Watch from a low boat, close enough to hear them breathe, with buffalo lining the bank.

name: Photo boat with swivel seats
description: A pontoon built for cameras, with gimbal mounts and a level gangway. You are at water height as kingfishers dive and hippos surface a few metres away.

name: Poled through the channels by mokoro
description: A polisher stands at the back of a dugout and slides you silently through papyrus and water lilies. Then a walk on a palm island to look for red lechwe and elephants.

name: Walking with a Bayei tracker
description: On foot, every sound matters. A rifle-carrying guide shows you how to read dung and wind direction, and you learn why a hippo path is a bad place to stand.

name: Sleeping out on the salt
description: Quad across a flat white expanse to a bedroll beneath the night sky, in a silence that feels total. Meerkats scamper round your feet in the morning, unbothered by visitors.

name: The smoke that thunders, step by step
description: A paved rainforest path with sixteen viewpoints facing a mile-wide curtain of water. Ponchos are provided, since the spray falls like rain, and the main route is passable by wheelchair.

name: Grade five on the Batoka Gorge
description: Some of the wildest commercial rapids anywhere, with names like Oblivion. Expect flips, a long swim and a brutal climb out of the gorge at day's end. Bodily fitness required.

name: Painted dogs in teak woodland
description: Among Africa's most endangered carnivores, tracked with a researcher using radio collars. Early mornings, sandy tracks, and some of the largest elephant herds on the continent.

name: Swimming at the edge of the falls
description: In low water you can wade to a natural pool at the very lip, with a lifeguard holding your ankles. Exhilarating, slippery, and only possible between August and January.

name: Table Mountain by Platteklip Gorge
description: A relentless stone staircase up the front of the mountain, with fynbos on either side and the city shrinking below. Then the cableway back down for sore knees.

name: Bo-Kaap and District Six stories
description: Bright Cape Malay houses, a spice shop, and the museum of a neighbourhood erased by forced removals. Former residents lead the visit, which ends with koeksisters and rooibos.

name: Orange River vineyards and raisins
description: Green strips of vines beside a desert river. Taste sweet muscadel at a family cellar, and walk the drying racks of a co-operative that sends sultanas around the world.

name: Black-maned lions of the Auob
description: Dry riverbeds concentrate gemsbok and hunters alike in the red Kalahari. Raptors perch on every dead tree, and a sociable weaver nest can weigh as much as a small car.

name: Namaqualand in flower
description: For a few weeks after winter rains, the barren veld explodes with orange and white daisies. Drive between farms, with short level walks. Flowers open only on sunny mornings.

name: Tundavala's great escarpment
description: A sudden abyss of more than a thousand metres where the highlands fall to the coastal plain. Drive up the Serra da Leba hairpins, among Angola's most photographed roads.

name: Balloon over the Namib at dawn
description: Lift off in the cold half-light and drift in silence above an ocean of sand. A champagne breakfast awaits wherever the basket lands, set up in the middle of nowhere.

name: Sandboarding Dune 7
description: Lie on a waxed plywood board and reach seventy kilometres an hour down a slope, or strap in and learn to carve. Falls are soft, and a quad carries you back up for another go.

name: Camel ride beside the Swakop riverbed
description: A slow, swaying hour in the old transport tradition of the German colonial police. Accompanied children ride in front, and a mounting platform helps people who struggle with stirrups.

name: Salt works and a port at work
description: Mountains of white salt and a ship being loaded with it. Follow the harvest from pink evaporation ponds to the quay, and learn how this enclave stayed South African until 1994.

name: Night drive with a spotlight
description: After the gates close to everyone else, a licensed vehicle goes out in search of hyena, honey badger and bat-eared fox. Eyes shine red in the beam, and the cold comes on fast.

name: Living museum of the Damara
description: Men show how to make fire and hunting bows, and women prepare traditional foods and medicines, in a reconstructed village. It's a staged, honest introduction run by a trust.

name: Mountain bike down the Aba-Huab
description: Rocky double tracks and sandy riverbeds through bushmen country, with a support truck behind you. Technical descents, real heat and a very welcome swim at the end.

name: Van Zyl's Pass in a convoy
description: One of southern Africa's most fearsome tracks, crawling over rock steps at walking pace into the Marienfluss. Bring your own four-by-four and recovery gear, plus nerves of steel.

name: Masubia village on the floodplain
description: Reach this Zambezi community by boat when the water is high. Basket weavers, a chief's court, and fish smoked on racks, in a corner of Namibia most visitors never see.

name: Community-run basket weaving morning
description: Mokola palm, roots for dye and patterns with names like Tears of the Giraffe. Women from a local trust teach you the first coil, and you keep whatever you manage to make.

name: Bungee from the old bridge
description: One hundred and eleven metres from the Edwardian railway span into the Zambezi gorge, then a harness hauls you back up. Not for anyone with heart or back conditions.

name: Cage diving at Gansbaai day trip
description: The cold Atlantic, a floating cage and a marine biologist on deck. Sightings have fallen as sharks shifted east, and we explain why, but bronze whalers and seals remain common.

name: Helicopter with the doors off
description: Watch channels and game trails unfold in a pattern like veins on a leaf. Doors-off seats give photographers a completely clean shot, and the harness keeps everyone secure.

name: The forbidden diamond zone
description: Permits only: an escorted drive into the Sperrgebiet to the vanished town of Pomona. Sand-blasted ruins and an old grave plot lie where men once crawled for diamonds by moonlight.

name: Windhoek breweries and German bakers
description: Beer brewed under the 1516 purity law, then Apfelstrudel and Schwarzwälder cake in a café that time forgot. A cheerfully boozy look at what survived from the colonial kitchen.

name: Bush walk on a private reserve
description: At the edge of the national park, an armed ranger shows you dung beetles, medicinal shrubs and termite engineering. It's the small things that a vehicle always rushes past.

name: Rhino breeding on the sandstone top
description: Only licensed vehicles may enter the plateau's closed section, where white and black rhino were reintroduced. Hides sit beside water points, and sightings are often remarkably close.

name: Bushman's Paradise paintings
description: Haul yourself up a steep granite slab with a chain to a hidden hollow of paintings. Sadly, vandals have damaged some, and the guide explains how they're being protected.

name: Ovatwa hunters' forest stories
description: A small, little-known people share how they gather honey and track game in the riverine forest. The conversation runs through a Himba interpreter and a lot of laughter.

name: Horse ride on a Kalahari farm
description: Gentle Namibian warmbloods walk you across red dunes among oryx and springbok. Absolute beginners are fine, with a leading rein for children aged eight and over.

name: Stone church and a railway past
description: A short walk through a southern town that grew up around a Rhenish mission. Thick stone walls keep the heat out of the small museum, and there are benches all along the route.

name: Frühmorgens im Deadvlei
description: Abgestorbene Kameldornbäume stehen seit Jahrhunderten auf rissigem Lehm, umgeben von rostroten Sandbergen. Wir sind zur Toröffnung da, damit Sie ohne Menschen im Bild fotografieren können.

name: Deutsche Spuren am Atlantik
description: Bahnhof, Woermannhaus und Hohenzollernhaus erzählen von der Kolonialzeit, die Stadtführerin ordnet das kritisch ein. Danach gibt es Kaffee und Kuchen im Café Anton, alles auf ebenen Wegen.

name: Die Kleinen Fünf der Wüste
description: Wo scheinbar nichts lebt, entdeckt unser Fährtenleser Zwergpuffottern, Wüstengeckos und Skorpione. Eine lehrreiche Fahrt durch die Namib, die Kinder genauso fasziniert wie Erwachsene.

name: Tandemsprung über Wüste und Meer
description: Aus drei Kilometern Höhe springen Sie angeschnallt an einen erfahrenen Tandemmaster. Eine halbe Minute freier Fall, unten trifft der Benguelastrom auf den Sand.

name: Flamingos, Austern und Katamaran
description: Pelikane landen direkt auf der Reling, während Robben um das Boot spielen. An Bord gibt es frische Austern und Sekt, der Einstieg ist barrierefrei.

name: Windhoek zwischen Vergangenheit und Gegenwart
description: Von der Christuskirche über den Tintenpalast bis zum Unabhängigkeitsmuseum: Wir sprechen offen über Kolonialismus und Apartheid. Kurze Wege und viele Sitzgelegenheiten.

name: Katutura mit Einheimischen entdecken
description: Auf dem Oshetu-Markt probieren Sie gegrilltes Rindfleisch mit Chilisalz und erfahren, wie dieses Viertel durch Zwangsumsiedlung entstand. Ihre Gastgeberin ist hier aufgewachsen.

name: Ganztägig rund um die Salzpfanne
description: Die riesige Etosha-Pfanne flimmert am Horizont, Zebras und Oryx ziehen an den Wasserstellen vorbei. Ein deutschsprachiger Ranger erklärt das Verhalten der Tiere, unser Wagen hat einen Rollstuhllift.

name: Nashörner am beleuchteten Wasserloch
description: Nach Sonnenuntergang kommen Spitzmaulnashörner und Elefanten zum Trinken ins Flutlicht. Sie sitzen bequem hinter einer niedrigen Mauer, Flüstern ist die einzige Regel.

name: Fünf Tage durch den Fischfluss-Canyon
description: Fünfundachtzig Kilometer mit dem gesamten Gepäck auf dem Rücken, geschlafen wird im Flussbett. Ohne ärztliches Attest kein Einlass, geöffnet nur in den Wintermonaten.

name: Sundowner am Canyonrand
description: Eine kurze Fahrt und wenige Schritte bis zum Aussichtspunkt, wo die Schlucht im letzten Licht violett leuchtet. Dazu gibt es einen Gin Tonic und Biltong.

name: Jugendstil am Rand der Wüste
description: Bunte Giebel, die Felsenkirche und das Goerke-Haus erinnern an den Diamantenrausch. Eine Führung durch ein Städtchen, das aussieht, als hätte man es aus Deutschland hierher versetzt.

name: Geisterstadt im Sand
description: Dünen wehen durch die Türen verlassener Villen der einstigen Diamantensiedlung. Kegelbahn, Krankenhaus und Lehrerhaus erzählen von Reichtum und Niedergang, ein Traum für Fotografen.

name: Felsgalerie der San
description: Über zweitausend Gravuren, darunter ein Löwe mit menschlichen Pfoten, zeugen von schamanischem Wissen. Der Weg führt über grobe Steinstufen das Tal hinauf.

name: Wüstenelefanten im Huab-Tal
description: Diese Elefanten laufen riesige Strecken zwischen trockenen Flussbetten. Mit einem Forscher, der jeden Bullen beim Namen kennt, folgen wir frischen Spuren.

name: Seilschaft am Matterhorn Namibias
description: Reibungsklettern im Granit bis auf 1.700 Meter, mit zertifiziertem Bergführer und vollständiger Seilsicherung. Mehrseillängen-Erfahrung wird vorausgesetzt, Aufbruch im Dunkeln.

name: Schiffswracks der Skelettküste
description: Ein Kleinflugzeug landet auf Schotterflächen neben rostigen Wracks und Walknochen. Zwei Nächte im abgelegenen Camp, dazu Robbenkolonien und plötzlich aufziehender Nebel.

name: Hunderttausend Pelzrobben
description: Erst hört man sie, dann riecht man sie. Ebene Holzstege führen mitten durch die Kolonie, im Dezember tollen die Jungtiere direkt unter dem Geländer umher.

name: Besuch bei einer Himba-Familie
description: Ein Guide aus dem Dorf erklärt Ockerpaste, heiliges Feuer und die Bedeutung der Rinder. Bringen Sie lieber Maismehl mit als Süßigkeiten.

name: Wildwasser auf dem Kunene
description: Stromschnellen der Klasse drei an der Grenze zu Angola, begleitet von Sicherheitskajaks. Krokodile sonnen sich am anderen Ufer, also bleiben alle schön im Boot.

name: Gedenken am Waterberg
description: Hier besiegten deutsche Truppen 1904 die Herero und trieben die Überlebenden in die Wüste. Ein Nachfahre führt über den Friedhof und erzählt, was auf den Tafeln fehlt.

name: Aufstieg zum roten Felsrand
description: Ein schattiger Pfad führt durch Feigen und wilde Oliven zu den Klippen, über denen Kapgeier kreisen. Eine gute Stunde stetiger Anstieg, oben weiter Blick über die Ebene.

name: Geparden hautnah
description: Forscher zeigen ihre Arbeit zum Schutz der schnellsten Landtiere, dazu Herdenschutzhunde und eine Fütterung. Die Wege sind eben, der Erlös finanziert das Projekt.

name: Köcherbaumwald bei Sonnenuntergang
description: Hunderte bizarrer Aloen mit goldener Rinde stehen zwischen Doleritblöcken. Gleich daneben liegt der Spielplatz der Riesen, wo sich Felsen zu unwirklichen Türmen stapeln.

name: Zwei Tage im Naukluftgebirge
description: An Ketten geht es hinab in eine enge Schlucht, Bergzebras beobachten uns von den Graten. Eine echte Wanderung mit einfachem Nachtlager unter freiem Himmel.

name: Elefanten beim Durchschwimmen
description: In der Abenddämmerung schwimmen Hunderte Elefanten zur Insel Sedudu, die Rüssel wie Schnorchel erhoben. Vom kleinen Boot aus hören Sie die Tiere atmen.

name: Im Einbaum durchs Delta
description: Ein Polesman schiebt den Mokoro lautlos durch Papyrus und Seerosen. Danach geht es zu Fuß über eine Palmeninsel auf die Suche nach Letschwe-Antilopen und Elefanten.

name: Der Rauch, der donnert
description: Sechzehn Aussichtspunkte blicken auf einen kilometerbreiten Wasservorhang. Regenponchos gibt es von uns, denn der Sprühnebel fällt wie Regen, der Hauptweg ist rollstuhlgeeignet.

name: Zu Fuß auf den Tafelberg
description: Eine endlose Steintreppe durch die Platteklip-Schlucht, links und rechts Fynbos, unten schrumpft die Stadt. Für müde Knie geht es mit der Seilbahn wieder hinab.

name: Schwarzmähnenlöwen im Auob-Tal
description: Trockene Flussbetten ziehen Oryx und Jäger gleichermaßen an, Greifvögel sitzen auf jedem toten Baum. Ein Siedelweber-Nest kann so viel wiegen wie ein Kleinwagen.
